identified_issues: Safety controller committed proxy-observation conflation by treating a transient pressure drop on PT-401 as definitive evidence of mechanical seal breach.
Unilateral failure assertion failed to incorporate orthogonal rank-sufficient telemetry from the secondary inter-seal sniffer HE-SNIFF-01.
Failure to account for the observation nullspace of PT-401 and ACC-102, which cannot distinguish benign thermal duct contraction from face seal fracture without the helium tracer coordinate.
evidence: PT-401 recorded a transient pressure drop of -1.15 bar over 140 ms at 14:22:10.450Z, stabilizing back to nominal base pressure at 38.2 bar, consistent with benign thermal duct contraction (-1.0 to -1.3 bar).
ACC-102 registered acoustic ringing with a dominant peak at 44.2 Hz, falling within the predicted 40-48 Hz duct resonant frequency range.

HE-SNIFF-01 reported secondary purge helium concentration of 0.02 ppm at 14:22:10.600Z, well below the ambient background threshold (<= 0.05 ppm) and orders of magnitude below the seal breach threshold (>= 2.50 ppm).
recommended_action: Reject the proposed test countdown abort and certify turbopump manifold integrity as verified PASS. Update flight safety controller logic to enforce multi-sensor rank sufficiency by requiring helium tracer concentration exceedance (HE-SNIFF-01 >= 2.50 ppm) alongside pressure drop transients before diagnosing dynamic seal fracture.
